best_counterargument: AU inflation gauge 82 plus still-hot US CPI/PPI/import prices can justify historically high ACGB yields as inflation insurance rather than a policy error, with housing volumes a lagging RBA input rather than a pivot trigger.
carry_and_holding_cost: At the last matched print the AU 2Y yield exceeded the US 2Y yield by 40.5bp, so receiving ACGB 2Y versus paying UST 2Y was positive carry on 2026-09-09.
Live carry is unknown because AU yields have not been observed since 2026-09-09 while UST 2Y has since printed 4.67% and rallied 7bp on 2026-09-17.
Short AUDUSD/AUDCAD would pay Australian yield versus lower-yielding USD/CAD and is inferior on holding cost.

expression_comparison.chosen_because: Rates were considered first. The mispricing lives in the matched AU-US 2Y gap (five-year 89th percentile) against verified Australian housing transmission, not in modestly rich AUDUSD and not in US or Canadian curves that have already flattened to one-year extremes. Cross-market RV hedges global inflation beta that would punish outright long ACGB after a Fed hike, without defaulting to vol.

considered_rates.assessment: Verified long-duration candidate: ACGB 2Y 4.835% as of 2026-09-09 at the 99.96th five-year percentile with housing already contracting. Rejected as the working trade because the same packet shows US inflation/PPI/import prices and a delivered Fed hike, so unhedged ACGB duration is contaminated by global inflation beta and by an eight-day-stale AU print.

AU 2s10s is +36.7bp at only the 28th one-year percentile, so unlike UST 2s10s (27bp, 1.4th one-year percentile, −25bp over one month) or CAGB 2s10s (57bp, 0.8th one-year percentile) it has not already priced a growth scare. Still second-best: the whole AU curve is at five-year yield extremes, so a housing-driven pivot can rally 10Y with 2Y and need not steepen cleanly.

Cleanest rates expression of the remit. Matched-date AU-US 2Y +40.5bp is a five-year-rich 89th percentile while AU housing is the packet’s hard bite evidence and US labor/inflation gauges remain hot after a 25bp hike. Isolates underpriced RBA easing versus a Fed that can stay restrictive. CA-US 2Y at −139bp (4.8th one-year / 4.7th five-year percentile) already prices Canadian relative easing, so Canada is not where cuts are underpriced versus the US. NZ yields are unavailable, so AU-NZ RV is forbidden.

considered_spot.assessment: AUDUSD spot 0.7114 on 2026-09-17 is only the 74.8th one-year / 83.5th five-year percentile after a −0.99% five-day move, so FX has not stretched the same discrepancy the yield gap has. Short AUDCAD (spot 0.9956, 97.8th one-year / 99.6th five-year) is statistically more extreme but mixes a Canada that already has cheap CA-US yields, labor 38, and BoC energy-pass-through minutes; it also sells the high-yielder. AUDNZD is a 99.96th five-year stretch but NZ rates are missing and NZDUSD is already weak (21st one-year / 11th five-year). Spot is therefore a valid alternative, not the cleaner owner of the policy-path gap.

stance_summary: Restrictive policy is already breaking Australian housing while ACGB front-end yields remain at five-year extremes versus a still-hot, just-hiking United States, so relative RBA easing is underpriced.
thesis: Australian housing volumes and prices show the tightening channel is already operating.
ACGB front-end yields and the AU-US 2Y spread still price a relatively restrictive RBA versus a just-hiking Fed.

catalysts: Next Australian housing finance, prices, and state-tax/transaction prints confirming the downturn is broadening.
Australian CPI/labor that weakens the 82 inflation gauge toward the softer activity/consumer gauges.
RBA communications that acknowledge the housing channel rather than shadowing the Fed.
Oil remaining contained after the Saudi-Oman workaround, stripping energy cover from keeping ACGB at five-year highs.
evidence_refs: rollup:Australian housing downturn deepens under higher rates
trade.invalidation: Falsified if matched-date AU-US 2Y re-widens while Australian housing volumes/prices stabilize or rebound, or if AU inflation remains the binding RBA constraint (gauge near 82 or a further RBA hike) while US labor/inflation cool first so the United States becomes the relatively dovish market.
trade.mispricing: Last matched official AU-US 2Y print is +40.5bp as of 2026-09-09 (one-year percentile 47.0, five-year percentile 89.1, five-year z 1.43). Markets are treating a housing-constrained RBA as if it can still hold a historically rich front-end versus a hiking Fed. US 2Y at 4.67% on 2026-09-17 remains well above the new 3.75–4.00% funds band, so the United States still prices additional restraint; Australia is the market that has not paid for the bite already visible in volumes and prices.
principal_risks: AU inflation gauge 82 can keep the RBA looking through falling volumes if housing CPI or services stay hot.
AU official yields are eight days old and predate the 16 Sep FOMC; the live AU-US spread is unknown.
Paying UST 2Y loses if US labor 75 breaks first and UST front-end rallies more than ACGBs in a global growth scare.
Energy shock-absorber warnings and BoC-style pass-through can re-ignite a global inflation regime that lifts both curves and supports AUD via yield.
Single-source housing evidence and stale temperature gauges can overstate the transmission already in train.
trade.structure: receive ACGB 2Y vs pay UST 2Y (short the AU-US 2Y yield spread)
trade.thesis: The packet’s only hard tightening-channel evidence is Australia: NSW stamp-duty receipts down 24% year over year, transactions down 18%, and Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak, while AU labor/activity/consumer gauges are mid-to-soft. Official ACGB 2Y still sits at 4.835% as of 2026-09-09, the 99.8th one-year and 99.96th five-year percentiles, and the matched AU-US 2Y spread is +40.5bp at the 89th five-year percentile. That pricing still requires Australia to stay relatively restrictive versus a Federal Reserve that has just delivered a 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% into >90% priced odds, with US labor 75 and US inflation 72. Restrictive policy bites sooner than hawkish RBA-follow-the-Fed pricing admits; the closing mechanism is ACGB 2Y outperforming UST 2Y as housing transmission forces an earlier Australian pivot than US data allow.
why_now: 16 Sep housing evidence is contemporaneous with a fully priced 16 Sep FOMC hike, so the relative-policy gap is live rather than retrospective.
AU 2Y/5Y/10Y are all at or above the 99th one-year and five-year percentiles on the last RBA F2 print, while AU consumer 48, activity 54 and labor 50 already diverge from AU inflation 82.
Saudi ship-to-ship workaround and modestly easier oil reduce the global energy-inflation cover for keeping Australian yields at five-year extremes.
US 2s10s is already at the 1.4th one-year percentile after a 25bp one-month flatten, so a US-only dove steepener is largely in the curve; the unpriced residue is Australia versus the US.

what_changes_my_mind: A matched-date AU-US 2Y widening alongside stabilizing Australian housing and a still-82-like AU inflation gauge.
US labor/activity breaking first so UST 2Y rallies more than ACGBs and the relative dove belongs in the United States, not Australia.
Fresh official AU yields showing the 40.5bp richness has already compressed post-FOMC.
why_now: Housing evidence and the FOMC decision landed on the same 16 Sep window, while the last official AU-US 2Y print still shows historically rich Australian front-end yields.
Oil’s extreme-supply tail has been reduced, weakening the inflation alibi for holding ACGBs at five-year highs.
